subject: Dedicated sizing: Alectro traffic sample + burst/latency constraints
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Maya Rao <maya.rao@alectro.com>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 30 Mar 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated sizing: Alectro traffic sample + burst/latency constraints

Hi Maya —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. As discussed, to give you a tight Dedicated sizing estimate we need a small traffic sample and a few clarifying answers about burst behavior and prompt/response shapes. I attached a short intake workbook; if it’s easier you can reply inline with the CSV sample you already export from your API gateway.

Quick asks (should take ~10–15 minutes):
- Sample: 24–72 hour CSV of requests (timestamp, endpoint, prompt_token_count, response_token_count, model_requested, status, latency_ms) — a trimmed sample is fine.
- Peak/burst: typical sustained qps and an observed peak 5–minute qps during events (if you don’t track 5-min, a 1-min peak is fine).
- Concurrency: how many concurrent sessions or active request tokens do you see in spikes (if you have session IDs).
- Streaming vs non-streaming: percent of requests that stream partial tokens.
- Latency SLO: p50/p95/p99 targets and what you consider a critical failure (e.g., >2s).
- Model mix: fraction using open Llama-family vs any specialized proprietary models; any plan to switch to quantized or smaller variants in prod.

If you prefer a call to walk through the intake, I can loop in Karthik (solutions) and Ben (sales). Goal: get a first-pass fleet footprint and a recommended GPU mix + fallback plan by EOD tomorrow.

Attachments: redwood_presales_intake.xlsx (workbook)

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Sr. Solutions Architect — Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0182

From: Maya Rao <maya.rao@alectro.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 30 Mar 2029 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing: Alectro traffic sample + burst/latency constraints

Hi Laura —

Thanks — attaching a small extract (alectro_traffic_sample.csv) with 48 hours of traffic. Quick answers inline:
- Sustained qps: ~45 qps during business hours (PST).
- Peak: we saw a 5-minute peak of ~720 qps during a product launch last month (outlier). Typical daily peaks are ~150–200 qps for 1–2 minute bursts.
- Concurrency: our platform keeps short-lived sessions; concurrent active requests during peak are ~120–160.
- Streaming: ~18% of requests are streaming (chat-like experiences).
- Latency SLOs: p95 = 600 ms, p99 = 1.1 s. For onboarding we can tolerate up to 2.5 s for non-critical requests; checkout flows must stay under 800 ms p95.
- Model mix: today ~70% small Llama-quantized; 30% larger renaissance-v2 (non-quantized). We plan to move 50% of renaissance-v2 to a 4-bit quantized variant in the next quarter.

Let me know if you need additional columns; I redacted user ids for privacy.

Cheers,
Maya Rao
Head of Product — Alectro Systems
maya.rao@alectro.com
+1 (650) 555-3344

Attachment: alectro_traffic_sample.csv

Fwding Maya’s sample — please review and give a first-pass Dedicated footprint and recommended GPU mix. Important constraints:
- Hard p95 target for checkout flows: <800 ms.
- Very large short-lived 5-min outlier (720 qps) — need fallback plan (model degradation or priority queues).
- Streaming ~18%: streaming requests increase per-request memory/KV cache pressure.

Ask:
1) Karthik — can you produce a quick sketch (GPU types, # nodes, KV/cache sizing, expected occupancy) and a short list of fallbacks (smaller quantized variant mapping) we can propose? Aim for a conservative and an optimized footprint.
2) Ben — pricing/commit options for reserved capacity and burst credits; ballpark monthly commit tiers we should show.

Timeline: proposal to Maya by EOD tomorrow (we have a demo on Tue).

Thanks — Laura

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.com
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.com, maya.rao@alectro.com
Date: Sat, 30 Mar 2029 15:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Dedicated sizing: Alectro traffic sample + burst/latency constraints

Thanks for the sample — dug into the CSV and sketched two candidate footprints. High-level notes and open questions below.

Conservative footprint (high availability / headroom):
- GPU mix: 8x A100-80GB (or equivalent L4x for cost-optimized inference) + 4x T4 for background batch/async tasks.
- Expected sustained throughput: 45 qps comfortably, occupancy 30–40% at p95 with batching.
- Burst handling: use autoscaling + burst credits to allow additional 6x A100-equivalent capacity for 10-minute windows. Fallback routing: route non-critical endpoints to quantized renaissance-v2-4bit variant.
- KV cache: provisioned Redis cluster (sharded) with ~120 GB of total KV cache to keep common prefixes hot (estimate from prompt mix).
- Network/replicas: active/standby across two AZs for latency SLAs.

Optimized footprint (cost-conscious):
- GPU mix: 6x L4x (8-bit quantized paths) + autoscale to 10x L4x on bursts.
- Streaming: reserve dedicated streaming lanes (1/5th of capacity) to avoid head-of-line blocking — streaming increases per-connection memory ~20–30%.
- Latency: can meet checkout p95 <800 ms with priority lanes + smaller model fallbacks for non-critical paths.

Open questions (need Maya confirmation):
- How many requests per minute need checkout-level priority during peak (percent of total)? We used 15% by default.
- For the 5-min 720 qps outlier: is that a one-off event (marketing push) you expect to repeat monthly? If recurring, we should size for a sustained monthly burst window or propose burst credits.
- Any hard regulatory/data residency constraints beyond US?

Next steps: I’ll convert this into a short one-page footprint (GPU counts, cost delta, recommended commit tiers) and Ben can attach commit pricing. Target: send consolidated proposal to Maya by 09:00 PT tomorrow.

-Karthik
